text_blocks.snippet: A professional roof inspection in Utah typically costs between $100 and $400, with most homeowners paying an average of $190 to $230 for a standard residential property.
However, many Utah roofing companies provide free basic visual inspections if you are actively seeking a repair or replacement quote.
The method used to check your roof heavily dictates the final price:

list.snippet:
Basic Visual / Physical Inspection ($75 – $200): The inspector walks the roof to look for missing shingles, exposed flashing, and standard wear. Local companies like Fortress Roofing
in Salt Lake City offer comprehensive physical packages around this baseline range.
Drone Inspection ($150 – $400): Used for steep pitches, complex layouts, or snow-covered roofs where walking is unsafe.
Real Estate / Insurance Written Reports ($200 – $400): Formal, documented summaries with photos required for home sales or insurance claims.
Infrared / Thermal Scanning ($300 – $600+): Specialized scans that locate hidden moisture traps, attic heat loss, or deep leaks beneath the surface.

Roof Pitch & Height: Utah's heavy snow loads mean many homes feature highly steep pitches. A steep roof (or a multi-story home) requires extra safety setup or drone gear, adding $25 to $150
to the base labor.
Home Size: A larger roof footprint requires more time to evaluate. Properties over 3,000 square feet typically scale up on a tiered pricing model.
Certifications: If you need a formal "Roof Certification" confirming the roof will last another 2–5 years for a home buyer, expect an additional $75 to $200 fee.

text_blocks.snippet:
If you suspect recent storm damage or a clear leak, reach out to local contractors like Vertex Roofing
or Homer Roofing
, who routinely offer no-obligation visual roof inspections to assess damage. You should only pay for an inspection if you require an independent third-party assessment, a certified insurance document, or a structural engineering report.

If you would like, I can help you find highly-rated roofing contractors in your specific Utah city or provide an estimate on roof repair costs if you already know what the issue is. Which option works best for you?
